LandingFeatures.heading: A platform built for both business and government
LandingFeatures.subheading: The system works automatically from data collection to notifications, reducing the burden on companies while increasing transparency for government.
LandingFeatures.collectDescription: Automatically pulls and filters software procurement announcements from e-GP and BMA agencies, with duplicate detection.
LandingFeatures.aiDescription: Vertex AI helps analyze and extract key details such as scope of work, qualifications, and budget, so you don't have to read through PDFs one by one.
LandingFeatures.matchDescription: Compares TOR requirements against your company profile and notifies you instantly when a suitable project appears (Match Score).
LandingFeatures.transparencyDescription: Lets the public search project data and helps the OAG detect price irregularities and below-standard competition more easily.

LandingStats.projects: Software projects in the last 12 months
LandingStats.footnote: Counted from the announcements in the system right now; a project with several announcements counts once.

LandingSteps.heading: Get started in 3 steps
LandingSteps.subheading: Simple, fast, no technical knowledge required
LandingSteps.step1Description: Specify your technology skills, company size, and expertise. Takes less than 5 minutes.
LandingSteps.step2Description: The system scans new TORs daily, compares them to your profile, and calculates a fit score.
LandingSteps.step3Description: Receive alerts, review details already summarized by AI, and submit your proposal ahead of competitors.

LandingCta.heading: Ready to get started?

MarketInsights.title: Who wins Bangkok's software work, and at what price
MarketInsights.subtitle: Built from published award notices and contracts: the companies that win most, winning prices against the reference price, and the agencies where competition is low.
MarketInsights.kpiProjectsHint: {named} name the winner · {total} awarded in total
MarketInsights.kpiDiscountNone: No project yet has both a winning price and a reference price or budget
MarketInsights.kpiBase: Set against a real reference price
MarketInsights.kpiBaseHint: {budget} more published no reference price and are set against the budget instead
MarketInsights.winnersSubtitle: Projects won, each project counted once
MarketInsights.bandsTitle: How far below the reference price winners bid
MarketInsights.bandsFootnote: Highlighted bars are projects won 15% or more under the reference price, a sign of price competition.
MarketInsights.colTopWinners: Top winners (share of this agency's awards)
MarketInsights.emptyBody: Once award notices or contracts are imported from e-GP or MEA, they show here.
MarketInsights.limitsTitle: What the data can and can't tell
MarketInsights.limitBids: Sources publish only the winner and the winning price, never the other bids. "Against the average" here means against the reference price, and a company's "win rate" is its share of an agency's awards.
MarketInsights.limitBase: The reference price is used where published, otherwise the budget. Awards under 30% or over 105% of that figure are left out, as they are usually one lot of a bigger project or a figure in the wrong unit.
MarketInsights.limitSpread: "Low" competition means one company won more than half of the agency's awards; "high" means nearly every award went to a different company. At least 3 awards with a named winner are needed.
MarketInsights.limitSources: Winner names come from e-GP contracts. MEA publishes only the agreed price, not the winner's name.
